conviction_note: Three independent, primary, correctly-dated series (NOAA CONUS temperature, BLS JOLTS construction hires, AHRI/Watsco industry shipments) all say the residential trades end market did NOT cool during the exact window ServiceTitan is about to report (fiscal Q2 = 1 May to 31 Jul 2026), which is the single risk the 4-Sep sell-side preview names and the one the +5.14 put skew is paying for; I haircut the +3.1pt finding sum to +2.5 because the three findings share one thesis, because short interest already fell 9.57m to 7.25m shares into the print so the squeeze fuel behind the historical +13.6/+12.9/+10.5 reactions is partly spent, because the company's own Q2 revenue guide of $284-286m sits BELOW the $287m consensus so an at-guide print still headlines as a consensus miss, and because the two most recent prints in the post-SaaSpocalypse derating regime paid only +4.13% and -6.41% versus +10-13% before it.

findings.finding: July 2026 was the warmest month in the entire 131-year contiguous-US temperature record (76.9degF, all 48 states above their 20th-century average, none near or below normal) and it is the final and seasonally largest month of ServiceTitan's fiscal Q2, which ended 31 July 2026 - record cooling load is the direct driver of the emergency HVAC service calls and same-day replacement tickets that flow through Gross Transaction Volume and the payments take-rate, i.e. the ~25% of revenue that is variable ($66.8m of the $268.8m reported in Q1 was non-subscription).
findings.why_not_priced: Nobody cross-reads NOAA NCEI into a vertical-SaaS name, and the coverage proves it: the 4-Sep-2026 preview of this print says the two metrics that will define the quarter are subscription revenue growth and margin progress, and treats trades demand only as a qualitative risk ('when demand in those trades cools, there is no other segment to absorb the impact'). If the record heat were priced there would be at least one published note tying GTV to July cooling degree days, GTV would be the named metric to watch instead of subscription revenue, and the front-month skew would not be paying 5.14 vol points for downside on a stock that just fell 13.66% in five sessions. GTV and take-rate are disclosed only in the release, so there is no interim print to have arbitraged this away.
findings.independence: AHRI industry shipments for June 2026 rose 21.7% y/y (central AC +26.8%, heat pumps +15.1%), the same physical demand pulse from a completely separate source - https://refindustry.com/news/ahri-reports-21-7-rise-in-u-s-ac-and-heat-pump-shipments/ (2026-08-19). Note this is the same THESIS as finding 3 below (end market did not cool) but rests on a different series and a different revenue line than finding 2.

findings.finding: ServiceTitan bills roughly $245-400 per technician per month, so its subscription line is mechanically a function of how many technicians its contractors employ - and BLS JOLTS shows construction hires in July 2026, the last month of ServiceTitan's fiscal Q2, at 366,000, up 14.7% month-over-month and 9.9% year-over-year, the highest construction hiring rate in about two years, with openings at 326,000 (+9.4% m/m).
findings.why_not_priced: The JOLTS release landed 2026-09-02, six days before the print, into a five-day window in which the stock fell 13.66% - so the tape moved hard the other way after the datapoint existed, which is what unpriced looks like. The seat-count-to-JOLTS link is also not in any coverage: the pricing model is per-technician but ServiceTitan does not disclose seats, so the sell-side models net dollar retention as a black box rather than as trades headcount. If this were priced, the >110% NDR line would be treated as de-risked rather than as the swing factor, and the 25-delta skew would not be paying for downside.
findings.independence: The BLS Employment Situation for August 2026 (released 2026-09-04) shows construction +22,000 with nonresidential specialty trade contractors +8,000, and ENR reports residential specialty trade contractors added 3,400 in August - a second government series, one month later, still positive: https://www.bls.gov/news.release/archives/empsit_09042026.htm and https://www.enr.com/articles/63625-in-august-specialty-trade-contractors-again-led-construction-industrys-hiring . Different mechanism and different revenue line from finding 1 (seats/subscription vs GTV/payments), same overall thesis.

findings.finding: The visible HVAC datapoint an analyst would cross-read into ServiceTitan is Lennox's 30-July print - residential revenue -7%, unit volume -12%, full-year growth guide cut from ~4% to ~1% - but that is a company-specific channel and share story (Lennox's own one-step volumes fell mid-teens, new construction -30%), while the industry-wide series over the same window went the other way: Watsco, the largest US HVAC distributor, reported domestic residential HVAC equipment sales +5% with unit volume +2% and ASPs +2% and titled its release 'further industry stabilization'; Lennox's own CEO said the repair-versus-replace trend 'has stabilized', and a repair-skewed market with record heat maximises job count and technician demand, which is what ServiceTitan monetises rather than equipment units.
findings.why_not_priced: TTAN carries only ~5 revenue estimates on an ~$8bn company, and the March-to-July wave of price-target cuts (Goldman $117 to $84, Citi $117 to $88, Truist $130 to $100, Canaccord $140 to $105, BTIG $130 to $105) was framed on multiple derating and AI cost, not on a reconciliation of Lennox against Watsco and AHRI. If the market had reconciled them, the residual bear case on TTAN would be purely the AI-seat-cannibalisation argument and the -29% drawdown from the 52-week high would not still be accompanied by a paid-for downside skew. Watsco's own stock fell ~15% on this release for a gross-margin reason, which buried the demand line inside it.
findings.independence: Lennox's own commentary is the counterparty to this finding rather than support for it - https://homepros.news/lennox-posts-12-drop-in-residential-unit-volume-cuts-full-year-outlook/ (2026-07-30). Same thesis as finding 1; treat the NOAA/AHRI/Watsco/Lennox cluster as one end-market cluster, not three.

searched_and_found_nothing: No S-1/S-3 resale registration, no announced secondary or follow-on offering, and no 8-K of any kind on EDGAR since 2026-08-01 - the only recent filings are routine Form 4s (CFO Dave Sherry sold at $90.02-92.01 on 2026-08-13/17), Form 144s dated 2026-08-04/11/12/14, a CEO intent-to-sell of 35,000 shares (~3.3% of his direct holding) filed 2026-08-04, and two Schedule 13G/13G/A filings. Insider supply is routine 10b5-1 distribution, small versus a 65.3m float, and fully visible in EDGAR, so it is priced.

ServiceTitan's own status page shows no incidents, 99.98% site and 100% mobile/core-feature uptime over the trailing 90 days - i.e. no peak-season outage to drive a churn or contractor-rage story either way.

No acquisition announced during fiscal Q2 FY27. The Convex, Conduit Tech and Schedule Engine deals surfacing in search are 2025 announcements (GlobeNewswire URL path /2025/09/18/) that closed in fiscal Q3 FY2026 - a relabelled-date trap I discarded.

The 'Carrier residential volumes down over 40%' figure that search served as current is Carrier's Q3/Q4 2025, not 2026 - discarded on date, and it would have inverted the finding had I used it. Likewise a widely-served 'YTD through July down 3.5% to 2,773,432 units' AHRI figure is the July 2025 release, not 2026.

Hiring-page teardown was inconclusive: ~11 pages of listings on servicetitan.com/careers, 62 US roles on Glassdoor, and no visible surge or deletion of a Max/AI onboarding team despite management naming onboarding capacity as the binding constraint on doubling Max locations again in Q2. One Enterprise Implementation Consultant listing was removed 2026-05-27; a single removal is not a team deletion and I dropped it.

Contractor-side churn evidence (Reddit price-hike threads, BBB data-export complaints, ServiceTitan-alternative comparison pages) is entirely SEO content-farm material with no dateable primary anchor, and price-increase grievances against ServiceTitan are perennial rather than new to this quarter.
Revelio Labs headcount data (3,529 employees, 444 postings) is only current through March 2026 - too stale to say anything about the May-July quarter.

No investor-conference appearance or intra-quarter management commentary between the 2026-06-04 Q1 call and today; last year's Pantheon investor session was 2025-09-18, so the 2026 user conference falls after this print.

Short interest is public and therefore priced: 7.25m shares, 7.60% of shares outstanding, 11.12% of float, 5.26 days to cover as of 2026-09-08, DOWN from 9.57m the prior month (https://stockanalysis.com/stocks/ttan/statistics/). I used it only to haircut my magnitude, not as a finding.
baseline_tension: Everything I found cuts directly against the baseline's priced lean: the 25-delta skew is paying 5.14 vol points for downside and the stock has given up 13.66% in five sessions and sits 29% below its 52-week high, while three independent primary series say the trades end market measurably strengthened inside the exact quarter being reported - so my number is positive but deliberately small (+2.5 against a 10.08% implied move and inside the 3.47% deadband), because the mechanism only touches revenue lines the market is no longer paying a multiple for, and the last two prints in this derating regime returned just +4.13% and -6.41%.
